title: Spend runway quick briefing — 1:1 prep + decision anchors
content:
Purpose: rapid prep for weekly 1:1 with Head of Product (Thu 3/11). Goal is to: 1) align on run-rate sensitivity for next two quarters, 2) present a shortlist of procurement items needing approvals, 3) surface tradeoffs + fallback options so we can decide in-meeting.

Top-line summary (for opening 2 mins):
- Base run-rate today (burn excluding one-offs): $7.9M/month. Cash cushion target (18 months): $142M.
- Requested near-term approvals this cycle: three items (~$1.1M one-time + $0.25M/mo recurring). Net runway impact if all approved: ~-1.8 months vs target.

Quick run-rate sensitivity (back-of-envelope):
- If recurring spend +$250k/mo, monthly burn -> $8.15M. On current cash + commitments, runway drops from ~18.0 -> 16.2 months.
- One-time capex $1.1M reduces available cash now; equivalent to ~0.14 months of current burn per $1M (check exacts with treasury).

Procurement items for decision (two-slide summary each):
A) Dedicated cluster capacity (reserved GPUs) — ask: approve $750k commitment (12 mo) to secure peak-season throughput.
- Why now: price lock & predictable latency for PLG growth.
- Upside: reduced per-token variable cost by estimated 18% at scale.
- Downside: capital commitment + risk if ARR growth misses target.
- Decision anchor: approve if product commits to 15–20% growth in API traffic next 6mo OR if ops can convert 25% of spot to reserved to hit payback <9mo.

B) Enterprise security audit & KMS integration — ask: $150k one-time + $20k/yr.
- Why: required by 2 enterprise pilots; failure to greenlight stalls deals.
- Decision anchor: approve if combined pipeline expected ARR > $250k in 12 months (conservative).

C) Monitoring/trace upgrade (vendor X) — ask: $200k one-time + $30k/yr license (replace in-house partial solution).
- Why: reduces MTTR for serving incidents and provides token-level cost attribution dashboards.
- Tradeoff: vendor lock + integration time (6–8 weeks).
- Decision anchor: approve only if we can reassign 0.5 FTE from infra to lead integration (reduces hidden ops cost).

Fallbacks / staged approvals (recommended):
- Option 1 (preferred): Approve A as a 6-mo pilot at 60% capacity commitment ($450k) with cliff review at 3 months tied to traffic thresholds. Approve B conditional on sales commit letters for two pilots (signed proof). Defer C until Q3 unless outage rates persist.
- Option 2: Defer A; negotiate lower minimum with vendor or convert portion to burst credits. Push B to final contract review with conditional funding.

Conversation prompts (short, to use live):
- "If product growth is 10% instead of 20% in six months, do we still want capacity locked?"
- "Which of these approvals unblock revenue in the next 90 days vs 180 days?"
- "What SLA/opt-outs should we require from vendor A to reduce tail risk?"

Notes to self (things to bring):
- One-pager with payback math + sensitivity table (attach).
- Short list of alternate vendors (names + ballpark pricing).
- Draft procurement approval language for CFO signature (pre-populate to save time).
- Ask legal to pre-approve standard security clauses for B and C to speed signing.

Open questions to resolve before meeting (quick ops tasks):
- Exact cash balance vs committed reserves (treasury) — Alex to confirm (due EOD Wed).
- Current projected ARR from pilots and expected close dates (sales) — Priya to pull pipeline notes.
- Spot vs reserved delta pricing sheet from infra vendor — Ethan to fetch.

Post-meeting follow-ups (if approved):
- Create PO and route to procurement (owner: me) — due within 3 business days.
- Add milestone to product roadmap for capacity onboarding + metrics (owner: Product Ops).
- Kick off security audit procurement + schedule vendor kickoff (owner: Security).

Decision record template (fill in in-meeting):
- Item, Decision (approve/conditional/defer), Approval conditions, Owner, Due date, Follow-up tasks.

Tone cues for 1:1: concise, options-first, bring numbers but be willing to propose a staged approach. Avoid long vendor history; focus on runway math + revenue unblock.

Misc scratch ideas (brain dump):
- Could we propose a convertible credit for A instead of all upfront? Ask vendor for credit option that converts to discount if usage > X.
- For B, explore co-funded audit with partner pilot customer (shared cost).

Last-minute checklist (30 mins before):
- Attach decks + one-pager, upload to shared drive, ping Head of Product with two sentence summary.
- Confirm treasury numbers.
- Print decision record template.

End.
